newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares stable on Wall Street's respite.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares stable on Wall Street's respite.

text.p: Singapore shares were mostly firmer on Wednesday morning, reflecting the overnight gains on Wall Street, dealers said.
At current levels, most Singapore blue chips were beginning to be attractive buys, especially the property and banking counters, they said.

"Property stocks have dropped about 10 percent from their highs a month ago and are good picks now," said a dealer with a European institution. He said City Developments, Keppel Land and DBS Land also posted strong 1996 profits. CityDev was among net gainers, rising S$0.30 (US$0.21) to S$13.10.

Other gainers included foreign tranches of banks like OCBC, UOB and DBS. At 0220 GMT, the benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index was up 2.45 points at 2,077.12. Market turnover was around 33 million shares with gainers outpacing losers by 116 to 50.

Drinks and property-linked Fraser & Neave led losers, shedding S$0.30 to S$11.90. Debutant Excel Machine, which saw over 7.9 million shares traded, was at S$0.64 after hitting a high of S$0.68 at the open against its IPO price of S$0.65.
